# Kvasir — Decentralized AI Inference (full site text)

Source: https://kvasir-ai.net/ · Engine: https://github.com/louisevandan/kvasir-net (BSL 1.1) · Last updated: 2026-09-21

This file is a plain-text mirror of the Kvasir homepage for LLM ingestion. All
claims are grounded in the p4 / Kvasir codebase. Compliance note: KVR is a
utility / contribution token on Solana devnet — not a tradable asset, price, or
investment; nothing here is a promise of financial return.

## Brand system

- p4 — the source-available engine: a control plane around the inference engine's RPC data plane, plus a peer-to-peer ring runtime. Discovers devices, plans layer and expert placement, launches workers, exposes OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible gateways. Source-available under the Business Source License (BSL) 1.1, on the `p4` branch.
- linkcpp — the previous engine, superseded by p4 in mid-2026. Results measured on it are labelled as such throughout this document.
- Kvasir — the network / product brand: the self-custody wallet + settlement gateway + node-reward network built on p4.
- KVR — the token. On-chain name "Kvasir", 6 decimals, Solana (devnet only). Used to pay for inference and to reward contributors.

One line: p4 is the engine; Kvasir is the network that turns it into a rewarded, decentralized AI inference marketplace paid in KVR.

## Hero

Headline: Bring compute. Earn KVR.
Kvasir binds scattered machines into one serving pool with p4, so no single node has to hold the whole model. Contribute a GPU, CPU or phone (NPU support in progress) and earn devnet KVR for the layers you run.
Badges: Runs on GPU · CPU · NPU · phone · OpenAI + Anthropic compatible · BSL engine · Solana devnet.

## Why decentralized AI (thesis)

AI shouldn't be owned by a handful of companies. Frontier inference is concentrating behind a few walled datacenters — closed weights, metered access, one bill paid to one owner. Kvasir is built the other way: open models served across a network of everyday devices, owned and earned by the people who run it. Stated plainly, because the difference matters: the engine and its settlement run today on our own fleet, and a device can already register, contribute and be paid — opening the serving ring itself to anyone is the next gate, not a thing already done.

Centralized AI: a few hyperscalers own the GPUs; models and infrastructure behind closed APIs; you rent access and value flows upward; opaque — you trust the operator.
Kvasir: any device joins a peer-to-peer ring — no central master on the data path; source-available p4 engine (BSL 1.1), inspectable; contributors earn KVR for the real compute they give; self-custody wallet — your keys never leave your device.

## The name (origin)

In Norse mythology, Kvasir was born when the Æsir and Vanir gods ended their war and made peace: each spat into a single vessel, and from their pooled essence rose the wisest being who ever lived — one who could answer any question. When he was slain, his blood was brewed into the Mead of Poetry, a draught that granted wisdom to everyone who drank it.
Why the name: pooled from every god and owned by none → intelligence assembled from many contributors' devices, no single owner. The wisest being answering any question → an open inference network anyone can query. A mead that shared wisdom with all → open access and KVR rewards to every contributor. On-chain, the token is named Kvasir (KVR) — the mead, distributed.

## How it works

1. Split — the model is divided into contiguous layer windows. Every device stores the same model but loads only its window; no node holds the whole thing. (Step-3.7-Flash 428B, 45 layers, placed as 16 stages.)
2. Serve — the request enters the ring. Each node runs its layers and passes only the hidden-state boundary to its neighbor; the last node samples the token and sends it back around — no central master. (ring runtime, OpenAI/Anthropic compatible.)
3. Reward — each node earns KVR weighted by the layers it ran (its share of the tokens produced), settled on Solana to that node's own wallet. (units += (out_tokens / 1000) × layer_share.)

## For contributors

Turn idle compute into KVR. Point a supported device at the network and it starts serving layers. You earn KVR proportional to the layers your node runs — your keys stay in your own wallet. Operator login is a Sign-In With Solana wallet signature with optional 2FA.

- Any device can join: GPUs, CPUs and phones run layers today, and NPU support is in progress. A peer-to-peer ring runtime lets each device hold just a few layers and pass only small boundary state to its neighbor — no gatekeeper, no single owner.
- Layer-share rewards: proportional to the layers your node runs, not vague participation. 1 unit ≈ 1k tokens × your layer share of each inference.
- Performance tiers: measured throughput sets a tier — S (×1.5), A (×1.25), B (×1.0), C (×0.7) — that multiplies your earned units.
- Uptime for infra roles: nodes filling infrastructure roles also accrue hourly uptime rewards.

Supported devices: GPU (CUDA · ROCm · Metal · Vulkan), CPU (x86-64 · ARM), NPU (on-device accelerators, in progress), Mobile (phones & edge via the ring runtime).

## For developers

One endpoint, backed by many devices. Keep your existing OpenAI or Anthropic client, point it at the Kvasir gateway, and pay per inference in KVR — no rewrites.

- OpenAI-compatible: /v1/chat/completions, /v1/models
- Anthropic-compatible: /anthropic/v1/messages, /anthropic/v1/models — non-streaming for now; a stream request is refused with a reason rather than answered in the wrong protocol
- Pay-per-call in KVR: quote → on-chain payment → inference (no API key)
- Prepaid credits with an API key (see below)
- Live model catalog aggregated from reachable bridges

Example:
curl https://gate.kvasir-ai.net/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KVR_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "model": "step-3.7-flash", "messages": [ { "role": "user", "content": "Explain layer-split inference." } ] }'

## Token & rewards (KVR)

KVR is the unit developers spend on inference and the unit contributors earn for the layers they run. Compute rewards are computed from measured work; infrastructure hosts also earn for uptime.
- Symbol: KVR (on-chain name "Kvasir", 6 decimals). Chain: Solana (devnet today). Pays for: inference (pay-per-request via the gateway). Rewards: compute (layer-share × performance tier).
- Self-custody wallet: keys live in the user's wallet (browser, desktop, or mobile), never with an operator; rewards are paid to each node's own owner wallet. On devnet, staked KVR and prepaid credits are held by the gateway treasury and tracked in its ledger until an on-chain staking program ships.
- Devnet, utility token: KVR currently runs on Solana devnet and is a utility / contribution token — not a tradable asset, price, or investment. Nothing here is financial advice or a promise of return.

## Network roles & rewards

Every role in the network earns KVR. The ring of compute nodes is fronted by the bridge and the settlement gateway; each is paid in KVR for what it actually does.
- Compute node (runs the model's layers): holds a few contiguous layers in the ring; earns per contribution unit (≈1k tokens served) × layer share × performance tier.
- Gateway host (public entry + settlement): serves the OpenAI/Anthropic gateway and settles KVR payments; earns hourly uptime + a ×1.5 bonus on every inference it helps serve.
- Bridge host: the HTTP face of the engine — it installs a session across a model's stages, submits to the head, gathers the token stream, and reports what each node contributed. It also serves the market a contributing device joins. It does not plan placement: which layers sit on which GPU comes from a plan an operator loads. Highest hourly uptime reward, because nothing reaches the ring without it.
Roles stack: one machine can be compute, gateway and bridge at once, and its rewards sum together — all paid in KVR to that node's own wallet.

Reward math: units += (tokens / 1k) × (node_layers / total_layers); effective = units × perf_tier × gateway_bonus; infra roles also earn hourly uptime (bridge rate > gateway rate), summed on top.
Performance tiers (by measured decode throughput): S ≥ 90 tok/s ×1.5; A ≥ 60 tok/s ×1.25; B ≥ 30 tok/s ×1.0; C < 30 tok/s ×0.7.

## Under the hood (p4)

p4 is the source-available engine that binds mixed hardware into one serving pool. Its ring runtime lets each device hold only a few layers and pass hidden state to its neighbor — no central master on the data path — while the inference engine data plane stays close to upstream with a small patch set.
- Ring runtime: every device stores the same model and loads only its layer window, opening one link to its predecessor and one to its successor; hidden-state boundaries circulate around the ring and the last rank returns the token — no central master on the data path.
- p4 control plane: the control plane the RPC data plane was missing. Discovers devices, plans layer and expert placement, launches the workers, exposes the gateways. A placement plan is an operator artifact — the engine does not load a model because an HTTP call asked it to. Source-available under the Business Source License (BSL) 1.1.
- Distributed layer placement: reads GGUF metadata and computes contiguous per-node layer windows via a rank manifest, plus optional MoE expert-FFN offload to node RAM.
- SIWS + 2FA security: for public deployments, operator access is a Sign-In With Solana signature over a server nonce, plus TOTP 2FA and single-use backup codes, on the gateway. A device that only wants to contribute compute does not sign in at all: it proves a wallet against the bridge and receives a token scoped to participation and nothing else.
The engine is source-available under the Business Source License (BSL) 1.1 — non-monetized internal use is permitted; hosted, embedded or revenue-generating use requires a commercial license: https://github.com/louisevandan/kvasir-net (distributed inference engine on the `p4` branch)

## Roadmap

- Now — Frontier-scale serving, live: Step-3.7-Flash, a 428B MoE, is placed as 16 stages across two AMD MI250 machines and is serving. A 122B model ran end to end across three physical machines — a GB10 and two Mac M4 Pros — one of them a phone holding part of it. Wallets on web/desktop/iOS/Android keep keys on the user's device.
- Live as of 2026-09-21 — the settlement gateway is ported to p4 and answering at gate.kvasir-ai.net. A paid request crosses the gateway, the bridge and the MI250 ring and is billed on the tokens it actually used; /v1/models answers 401 without a key, which is the gateway working rather than an outage. Measured on the serving ring the same day: Step-3.7-Flash (428B MoE) across two stages at 28-31 tok/s single stream, 270-285 ms to first token.
- In flight — the ring is going through recovery gates after an interrupted 64-request run; the desktop client is becoming a node that supervises a p4 agent rather than only registering one; and expert-grain sharding is being carried onto p4 — the market and the relays that let a phone join are live and credited, the shard download and the engine-side dispatch are not written yet.
- Coming — Kimi K3 (2.8T MoE) verification on p4, and the GLM-5.2 (744B) report from linkcpp published.
- Coming — Mainnet & on-chain settlement: everything today runs on Solana devnet with an off-chain settlement service; an on-chain rewards program and mainnet are planned.
- Coming — A permissionless global network: current demos ran on one operator's hardware; opening the network so anyone, anywhere can plug in a device and earn (no gatekeeper) is next.

## Verified on our test fleet

- 428B MoE serving today: Step-3.7-Flash across two AMD MI250 machines, placed as 16 stages.
- 122B params served end to end across 3 physical machines, with cosine similarity ≥ 0.9999 across ROCm, CUDA and a phone CPU.
- 4 separate node wallets, each credited for its layer share (test fleet).
- 2 API surfaces — OpenAI + Anthropic compatible.
- 4 wallet platforms — web · desktop · iOS · Android.
Summary: Step-3.7-Flash 428B on two MI250 machines · 122B end to end across three machines · OpenAI + Anthropic compatible · wallets on web/desktop/iOS/Android · Solana devnet.

## Inference API — self-issue an API key (for agents)

A native OpenAI-compatible endpoint with a prepaid-credit API key. An AI agent holding a Solana wallet secret can obtain a key headlessly (no browser). The gateway is live at https://gate.kvasir-ai.net; a call without a key answers 401, which is the gateway working rather than an outage.

- Base URL: https://gate.kvasir-ai.net/v1 · Auth: `Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>`
- Model: `step-3.7-flash` (Step-3.7-Flash, 428B MoE); `GET /v1/models` to list. Streaming (SSE) and native tool_calls are supported.
- SIWS signing: sign the challenge `message` string verbatim with the wallet's ed25519 key; submit the 64-byte signature as base64. `wallet` is the base58 public key.

Self-issue flow:
1. `POST https://gate.kvasir-ai.net/api/credits/register/challenge {"wallet":"<W>"}` -> `{nonce, message}`
2. sign(message) -> `POST /api/credits/register {"wallet","nonce","signature"}` (200 = self-registered onto the whitelist; 403 = self-register closed, an operator must approve)
3. `POST /api/credits/challenge {"wallet":"<W>"}` -> `{nonce, message}` (403 = not whitelisted)
4. sign(message) -> `POST /api/credits/apikey {"wallet","nonce","signature","label":"agent"}` -> `{apiKey}` (returned once — store it)
5. Use `apiKey` as an OpenAI Bearer key at the base URL. Check credit with `GET /api/credits/balance` (Bearer) -> `{balance, spent, symbol}`.

Pricing: `basePrice + tokens × perToken` KVR (currently `0.01 + tokens×0.00002`), Solana devnet. Insufficient balance -> HTTP 402; top up by transferring KVR to the treasury, then `POST /api/credits/deposit {wallet, amount, signature}`.
Runnable self-issue scripts (TS/Node, Python), the streaming + tool-call examples, and an interactive issuer are on the developer page: https://kvasir-ai.net/docs/api
